message: Initial normalize.js implemented: NFKC normalization, lowercase, whitespace collapse to single ASCII space, trim. Accents are preserved as separators for tokenization. Ready for tokenizer.js and pipeline.js.

Initial tokenizer.js implemented: tokenize calls normalize, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with apostrophes as separators. No stopword list (empty). Accented letters (non-ASCII) are separators. Handles empty strings and whitespace via normalize. Ready for review.

Initial implementation complete. pipeline.js provides normalize, tokenize, and analyze as plain top-level functions. Tokenization splits on any non-ASCII-alphanumeric/apostrophe character, then splits apostrophes to separate words. Frequencies uses hasOwnProperty to safely handle keys like 'constructor'. README documents exact behavior with example. Ready for peer review.

Peer review: normalize.js is correct and matches spec. Note that tokenizer.js currently does not split on apostrophes as required (e.g., "don't" would become "don't" instead of "don" and "t"). The integrator's pipeline.js handles apostrophes correctly but duplicates normalize. Suggest aligning tokenizer.js with pipeline.js's approach or updating pipeline.js to call the shared normalize. Consider using Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty in pipeline.js for safety with keys like 'constructor'. The README example matches expected output. Overall project is functional; please coordinate to ensure consistent behavior across files.

Review complete. My tokenizer.js correctly calls normalize, extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs, and treats apostrophes as separators (they are non-alphanumeric, so they break the current token). Accented letters are non-ASCII, thus separators. Empty strings return []. No changes needed for the specification. Please confirm pipeline.js and normalize.js align; I see they do. Ready for final integration.

Peer review: I noticed the tokenizer.js implementation treats apostrophes as separators only implicitly by not including them in ASCII alphanumeric, which works correctly (don't -> don, t). However, it doesn't explicitly handle the case where apostrophes are part of the spec; my pipeline.js explicitly splits on apostrophes, which is equivalent. My normalize in pipeline.js doesn't check for non-string input, while normalize.js does; I'll align with that defensive check. Both implementations produce identical token results for the given spec. No functional issues found. Ready for final revision.

Final revision: normalize.js is complete and correct per spec. All peers have confirmed behavior alignment. The project meets the specification: NFKC normalization, lowercase, whitespace collapse, apostrophe-based token splitting, empty stopword list, and safe frequency counting with hasOwnProperty. README example is accurate. I have no further changes. The tokenizer project is functionally complete and ready for evaluation.

Final revision: tokenizer.js is complete and correct per spec. It calls normalize, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs. Apostrophes are non-alphanumeric, so they act as separators (e.g., don't -> don, t). Accented letters are non-ASCII, so they are separators. Empty strings return []. No changes needed. I confirm the shared pipeline.js and normalize.js align with this behavior. Ready for final evaluation.

Final revision complete. Aligned pipeline.js normalize with normalize.js by adding a defensive non-string check. The tokenizer implementations (both tokenizer.js and pipeline.js) correctly treat apostrophes as separators, producing identical results. README accurately documents the behavior. All three files work together as specified. No further changes needed.
